_help: Your relay defaults, used by the 'relay' command, the Herdr 'Start AI relay' dialog and agents' 'relay' setup. Anything you choose when starting a relay overrides these. team: which team runs by default. teams: roles in order; each role has a job, a default agent (claude | codex | antigravity) and effort (low | medium | high | xhigh | max | default); once = first pass only; judge = approves or asks for changes (default: the last role). strengths: what each agent is good at; queue mode picks each task's agents from these. effort: 'recommended' (each role's own effort), 'none' (agent defaults) or 'role=level,...'. model: 'default' or 'role=name,...'. The executor always runs at high effort or above. codexApproveForMe: Codex stages start with --approve-for-me (no repeated git approval prompts). codexWindowsSandbox: the Windows sandbox Codex stages run in (-c windows.sandbox=<value>; default 'mxc'; 'none' = leave it to your Codex config). overnight: settings for unattended -Overnight runs (see its own _help). To add a team, copy _exampleTeam into teams under a name of your own (e.g. "docs").

coding.job: Write or update the task file .ai/tasks/T-xxx.md (goal, approach, files, acceptance criteria). No production code.
Implement the task file. Do not change its acceptance criteria; note any deviation in its Notes.
Test against the acceptance criteria in the task file, write tests, fill in its Test report. Report bugs instead of fixing production code.
Review the changes against the task file and .ai/DECISIONS.md and write your findings in its Review.

_exampleTeam.job: Outline the document in .ai/tasks/T-xxx.md: sections, audience, sources. No final text.
Write the document from the outline. Keep to the outline's sections.
Check the text for accuracy and clarity; list what must change in the task file's Review.

strengths.claude: planning, architecture, code review, tricky logic, writing
strengths.codex: static assets (images, icons, illustrations via image generation), scripts, tests
strengths.antigravity: app code, UI and full features, refactors

overnight._help: Used with -Overnight (or the Overnight box in the dialog). skipPermissions: start every agent with its permission checks off (claude --dangerously-skip-permissions, codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox, agy --dangerously-skip-permissions). until: no new task starts after this time ('08:00'), or 'done' = no time limit. maxCycles: plan-and-run cycles in queue mode, 0 = no limit. Whichever limit comes first ends the night; it also ends when nothing worthwhile is left. stallMinutes: no progress for this long = nudge, then skip. maxStageMinutes: a stage is interrupted after this long.

fallback._help: What the relay does when an agent's plan quota runs out (D-027). enabled: false = only wait, as before. waitMinutes: a limit that resets within this many minutes is waited out; a longer one makes the relay switch. models: each agent's model chain, best first (short names: antigravity hydrogen | flash | opus | sonnet | gpt-oss, claude fable | opus | sonnet | haiku, codex sol | astra | terra | luna). Antigravity's Gemini models (hydrogen, flash) share one quota, so its chain moves to Antigravity's Claude models and GPT-OSS. A model out of quota is switched inside the running session (no work lost); when an agent has no model left, another agent takes over the stage (agents: who to try, in order). basicModels may only test, never plan, build or review. lowerEffortAtPercent: when Claude's or Codex's plan use is at least this high, the roles in lowerEffortRoles start one effort step lower (tester down to low; reviewer only in fix rounds, down to medium). The executor and planner never lose effort. Quota planner (D-029): maxWaitMinutes = no stage waits longer for a quota, then it switches; claudeReservePercent = above this share of Claude's 5-hour limit new stages go to other agents, so your own Claude chats keep working (the judge may use Claude up to judgeClaudePercent); predict = before a stage, skip an agent whose plan probably can't finish it (learned from usage/model-stats.jsonl) when its reset is more than maxWaitMinutes away; allOut 'free-models' = when every agent and the OpenRouter budget are out, go on with free OpenRouter models (any role, flagged), 'wait' = wait for the first reset.

opencode._help: OpenCode on OpenRouter models (D-028). models: per role, best first; the relay takes the first one OpenRouter lists right now with tool calling, that has quota left and that the budget allows, and uses its free ':free' variant when one is listed and the project may use free models. freeModelProjects: project folder names that may use free models (their providers may keep prompts), or 'all'. budgetStopPercent: paid models stop when the key has used this much of its OpenRouter limit; free ones go on. budgetPace: 'weekly' = paid models may only use the share of the monthly limit for the weeks passed so far (unused weeks carry over), 'daily' the same per day, 'none' = only the limit. Every stage of every agent is recorded in usage/model-stats.jsonl; tools/model-report.ps1 turns it into the model report and suggestions (weekly task 'AI relay model report').

scout._help: The model scout (tools/model-scout.mjs, D-032) grades OpenRouter models for OpenCode from credible sources (OpenRouter's data incl. Artificial Analysis and Vals indexes, Terminal-Bench; SWE-bench and Aider only while recent) plus our own benchmark (tools/model-bench.ps1) and real relay results. autoPromoteRoles: roles whose list it may change by itself, only on measured evidence; other roles get a proposal you accept in the panel. minMargin: points a challenger must lead by. goodEnough: a measured first choice at or above this gets no paid challengers. trialEvery: 1 in this many tester stages tries the scout's trial model (free models, projects that allow them). paidBenchCapUsd: most a paid benchmark stage may cost (estimated); maxPaidBenchPerWeek: paid models measured a week. sourceMaxAgeDays: older sources are skipped. maxOutPricePerM / minContext: what counts as a candidate.

selection._help: Model selection (D-034, docs/model-selection.md). Per stage, agent + model + effort come from five levels, most specific first: stage ('relay switch') > task (its 'Relay:' line) > run (-Profile, -Stages/-Loop, -Model, -Effort) > project (.ai/relay-profile.json, its 'default' profile) > global (this block's 'profile', then the team's agents and efforts). A spec is agent[:model][@effort] (claude:sonnet@high, codex:sol, opencode:deepseek, haiku@low); 'a|b' is a chain tried in order, the first that fits now (quota, budget, listing) runs. profile: the global profile ('team' = the team's agents). agentModels: the model an agent gets for a role when no level names one. catalog: the exact version behind each short name (claude sonnet = claude-sonnet-5-5); dominated: versions outclassed on price or quality (used only when named, with a warning). profiles: named role sets; 'extends' builds on another; 'role.recheck' = the model for small fix-round re-checks. stepDown: in fix rounds whose code change is at most maxChangedLines, the roles listed step one model down the ladder (never below floor; never the executor or planner; not after a missed or free tester). escalate.tester: who tests after a tester passed work the judge then failed. budget: OpenRouter money per run (runCapUsd) and per stage (stageCapUsd); a paid OpenCode stage expected or seen above it is not started or is handed to a plan agent; .ai/relay-profile.json 'budget' overrides it per project. typicalTokens: per role, for cost estimates before a model has history. watchdog.stallMinutes: no change on screen this long = nudge, then hand over (day and night). skipExecutorWhenDone: skip the executor when the task's work is committed and nothing was asked for. keepAwake: keep the PC from sleeping while any relay runs.

catalog._help: API price per 1M tokens (in/out) for reference and the report; plan agents use your plan quota, not this money.

fable.use: hardest problems only; needs extra credits

selection.valueNotes: Claude Opus 5.5 = best planner and reviewer; Sonnet 5.5 = best everyday coder and tester; Haiku 5.5 = cheap checks and small re-checks; Fable 5.2 = only the hardest problems (needs credits); paid OpenRouter models resend about 200K tokens of context every step, so keep them to testing and small fixes

simple-site._use: small static site or landing page: few files, low risk

content-site._use: multi-page content site: page copy, SEO, facts and claims to check

pwa-app._use: PWA or front-end app: UI state, offline, client logic

full-app._use: full app with a backend: data model, auth, APIs, payments

bulk-content._use: many similar items: product copy, translations, data entry

hard-debug._use: a bug that resisted normal fixes, or a risky core change

ui-heavy._use: visual and layout work: components, styling, responsive pages

release._use: the last check before going live: strict tests and review

assets._use: images, icons, illustrations, brand files (Codex generates images)

projectTypes._help: D-035. The planner classifies a new project as one of these (complexity S|M|L, risk low|medium|high) and writes .ai/relay-profile.json: {"projectType", "complexity", "risk", "default": <profile>, "budget"}. profile = the role set for tasks without labels; typical = the task kinds such a project usually needs, in order; budget = OpenRouter money per run.

landing.use: one page that sells one thing: hero, sections, a form

brochure.use: a few static pages about a business

content-site.use: many pages of copy, SEO, facts and claims to check
content-site.typical: ui, content, bulk, assets, integration, deploy

blog-cms.use: posts or pages managed through a CMS

ecommerce.typical: data, backend, ui, integration, tests, deploy

booking.typical: data, backend, ui, integration, tests, deploy

web-app.use: a SaaS or tool with accounts and its own logic
web-app.typical: data, backend, logic, ui, tests, deploy

pwa.use: installable front-end app, offline, client state

dashboard.use: admin or analytics screens over existing data

api-backend.use: an API, worker or service without much UI

redesign-migration.use: moving an existing site to a new stack or design without losing anything
redesign-migration.typical: research, ui, content, data, tests, deploy

bulk-content.use: many similar items: product pages, translations, data entry

brand-assets.use: logos, images, icons, social and print files

kinds._help: D-035. The planner labels every task 'Labels: kind=<kind>, size=S|M|L, risk=low|medium|high'. Each kind's role chains cover all four agents (a|b = next if a doesn't fit now; a~b = equally good: the one with the most quota left goes first). The daily tuner (tools/selection-tuner.ps1) may reorder them per kind in usage/selection-tuning.json; risk and size rules apply on top.

content.use: page copy, headings, SEO text, legal pages

bulk.use: many similar items in one task

assets.use: images, icons, illustrations, favicons, OG images

backend.use: server code, auth, APIs, workers, payments

data.use: data model, schema, migrations, seed data, CMS models

integration.use: forms, CRM, email, analytics, third-party APIs

deploy.use: hosting, CI, domains, environment, build config

bugfix.use: a defect with a known symptom

research.use: investigate, compare options, audit an existing site

risk._help: Applied on top of the kind (D-035). high = mistakes are expensive (payments, auth, data loss, legal claims, going live); low = easy to see and undo.

size._help: L tasks (and high-risk ones) get a refiner stage before the executor, and the executor thinks at xhigh.

refiner._help: The task refiner (D-035): before the executor of a Size L or Risk high task, it sharpens the task file (approach, files, acceptance criteria, test plan, pitfalls). No production code.
refiner.job: Sharpen the task file before it is built: a concrete approach, the files to touch, testable acceptance criteria, a test plan and the pitfalls. Write no production code.

planner._help: The project planner's effort: xhigh when .ai/relay-profile.json says complexity L or risk high (D-035).

explore._help: D-035. 1 in 'every' low-risk tasks (not Size L) tries one model cheaper for the listed roles, on plan agents only (never paid OpenRouter, never the reviewer). The tuner learns from these tries.

tuner._help: tools/selection-tuner.ps1 (daily, by the supervisor). Only with minSamples per kind/role/model. Safe changes it applies itself: demote a model whose stall or miss rate reaches demoteRate; move a cheaper plan model before a dearer one when it does at least as well. Anything that costs more becomes a proposal (Accept/Dismiss in the panel) when it is at least 'margin' better. Changes live in usage/selection-tuning.json, every one in usage/selection-ledger.jsonl, undone with -Rollback <id>.

permissions._help: D-036. Projects whose relays start every agent WITHOUT permission checks in the daytime too, as overnight runs do (Claude and Antigravity --dangerously-skip-permissions, Codex without its sandbox, OpenCode --auto): the agents then run any command and change any file without asking. skipProjects: project folder names or full paths, or "all". One run instead: ai-relay.ps1 -SkipPermissions; -KeepPermissions always keeps the checks. Only here (your own file), never in a project's .ai/relay-profile.json, which agents write.
